scope: whole repo (src/lib/LibLeakyBucket.sol: leak, levelAt, headroomAt, fillAt, fillableAt; src/lib/LibLeakyBucketCheckpoint.sol: pack, unpack, levelAt, headroomAt, fillableAt, fill, plus the width constants and error identities; README and NatSpec as intent oracle)

summary.notes: Two rounds, looped until dry: 43 behaviours in round 1, then 6 more (error identities and the packed width constants) in round 2, which added no new gap. Round 2 ran after the round 1 coverage test landed on the branch, but every round 2 kill is credited to a pre-existing test by name, so attribution holds. Single survivor across both rounds was LibLeakyBucketCheckpoint.fillableAt, never exercised with a stored checkpoint differing from the queried clock; the one embedding test reaching it calls it in the same second as the mint, where the substitution is a no-op. Behaviour correct as written, so closed by strengthening testPackedReadsMatchCore in place plus a concrete-second case. Both adversarial findings are in the packed codec and neither is reachable through a monotonic block.timestamp: #1 is a write-path violation of the documented 'never hands out more headroom than reality' property (a timestamp behind the stored checkpoint regresses it; measured 501 units of headroom where 1 was earned, from a single zero-amount call), #2 is headroomAt/fillableAt disagreeing with fill when capacity exceeds LEAKY_BUCKET_LEVEL_MAX (fails closed, reverts on packing width rather than the documented capacity error). publishedTag is null: nothing is published yet, the next-v0.1.0 tag is an unconsumed version seed and the Soldeer project does not exist. testsAfterCommit is the coverage commit on branch mutation-test/leaky-bucket, pending merge of PR #3.

scope: re-probe of the whole repo after fixing the two findings from the 2026-09-21T18:05 scan: the checkpoint monotonicity fix in LibLeakyBucketCheckpoint.fill (#1) and the checkCapacity rejection of a capacity above LEAKY_BUCKET_LEVEL_MAX at every packed entry point (#2)

summary.notes: Fix pass rather than a discovery scan, so the two findings were already known and no new candidate was raised. All 49 prior mutants re-probed and still killed; M42/M43 retargeted to the new multi-line fill body. Ten new mutants cover the new behaviour and all are killed, including M50, which restores the exact defect filed as #1 (fill storing the raw clock) and is killed by testBackwardsClockBanksNoCredit and testFillBehindTheCheckpointGrantsNoHeadroom. Verified independently of the agent that produced the fix: full 59-mutant probe re-run against the committed tree, 59/59 killed, 0 survived, 0 no-run, 0 harness errors, on a green 62-test baseline. Known probe-config wart, not fixed here: the fail-pattern in mutants.toml does not name killers when the revert reason itself contains a bracket, which is why several checkCapacity mutants show KILLED with no named killer.
